extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers/authors preparing/submitting manuscripts to Forum of Mathematics, Sigma
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Forum of Mathematics, Sigma
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and journal information for authors who plan to submit research manuscripts to the open‑access mathematics journal Forum of Mathematics, Sigma. Covers scope, editorial organisation, and procedural notes about the submission system and author instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject scope / editorial clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are made by dedicated clusters of editors concentrated in the following areas: foundations of mathematics, discrete mathematics, algebra, number theory, algebraic and complex geometry, differential geometry and geometric analysis, topology, analysis, probability, differential equations, computational mathematics, applied analysis, mathematical physics, and theoretical computer science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification exists to aid the peer review process. Contributions which do not neatly fit within these categories are still welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access and peer-review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Forum of Mathematics, Pi and Forum of Mathematics, Sigma are an open access alternative to the leading specialist mathematics journals and offer fully open access publication combined with peer-review standards set by an international editorial board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong research papers from all parts of pure mathematics and related areas will be welcomed. All published papers will be free online to readers in perpetuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system account requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You will need an account for the submission system, which is separate to your Cambridge Core account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For login and submission support, visit the submission and support pages. Click 'Proceed to submission system' to continue to the partner submission website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author instructions / preparing your materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Please review this journal's author instructions, particularly the preparing your materials page, before submitting your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the journal's detailed author instructions and the 'preparing your materials' guidance to ensure submissions meet the journal's procedural and formatting expectations prior to using the submission system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial oversight / board calibre
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions are backed by an international editorial board of the highest calibre and supported by Cambridge University Press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect decisions to follow the standards and judgment of an international editorial board; the statement signals high editorial expectations though the page does not list specific evaluation criteria (e.g., novelty, significance, correctness).
